To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AI age is here, and that it is not benign.
AI is an important and growing technology in medicine, but that it has the potential to dehumanize the doctor-patient relationship.
the use of AI technologies in medical education is a double edged sword.
In summary, our research is concerned with
exploring the pedagogical and conceptual challenges of the AI age, and how we can best prepare medical students to navigate this new landscape.
the ethical and practical challenges of integrating AI into medical practice, education and training.
the ways that AI can be harnessed in medical education and practice, and how this can be done in ways that do not dehumanise patients or clinicians.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AI has revolutionised medicine, but it has also brought with it a new set of ethical and practical challenges that we are only beginning to understand.
AI has a role to play in medical education, but it is not a replacement for clinical experience and the human touch.

AI is a powerful tool that needs to be integrated into medical education, not as a panacea but as a tool to be used in a balanced and nuanced way, with an understanding of the ethical and practical issues it raises.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AI has a place in medicine, but not a place above medicine.
we are trying to understand the impact of technology on the doctor-patient relationship, and to understand what this means for the way we educate medical students.
AI has the potential to be an important tool for medical education, but only if it is used with caution and awareness of its limitations and pitfalls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rise of AI in medicine needs to be accompanied by the rise of the humanities, to counter the reduction of medicine to a technology of problem solving.
the medical education community needs to be more aware of the potential pitfalls of AI and to be more proactive in shaping its future.
AI is not a panacea, but a powerful tool for enhancing medical care, but only if used with care.
